verdict.reasoning: The patient opens with: "I keep having a headache."
Onset and timing are stated: "It started yesterday" and later "Yesterday, about mid morning."
Location and quality: "It's on the left side at the back" and "Just quite intense and kind of quite throbbing."
Pain score: Doctor asks 0–10 scale; patient replies, "Say about 8."
Patient denies associated symptoms: "No, nothing" to nausea/vomiting/tingling/weakness, "No" to blurred vision, "No" to fever, and "No" to rashes.
Medication and response: "I took some Nurofen yesterday." and when asked if it helped, patient says, "Not really."
When asked about past headaches, patient states: "Not really." indicating no prior significant history of headaches.
Family history: "My mother's had hypertension and she does get migraines."
Social history: "Who do you live with at home?" Patient: "My partner." and later: "I'm a designer."
Substance use: "And do you smoke at all normally?" – "No, I don't."; "Do you drink any alcohol regularly?" – "No."; "And any other drugs?" – "No."
The entire consultation concerns a new-onset headache starting yesterday, consistent with an acute headache presentation.
Unusual and resistant: Patient states, "It's unusual for me to have a headache," and reports taking Nurofen with "Not really" any effect.
Doctor’s plan: "trying slightly stronger pain relief. So similar to ibuprofen, but taking it instead of ibuprofen, not at the same time."
Doctor adds: "You can take paracetamol along with that." indicating concurrent use with the new pain relief.
Supportive care: "Try and take rest, have lots of good hydration."
Safety netting: "if the pain's getting worse or you get new symptoms, feel fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness... then we need to speak to you."
Follow-up timeframe: "if it's getting worse or not settling in the next day or two, then certainly give us a call back."
